02

Synthesis protocolOrdered operations, material dependencies and stage-specific conditions

01
characterization

Dilute hexane dispersion and drop-cast on acetone-cleaned glass

Dilute hexane dispersion and drop-cast on acetone-cleaned glass. Dilute hexane dispersions until individual dots resolve, then drop-cast on acetone-cleaned glass coverslips. Numerical dilution and deposited volume are absent. Missing fields: dilution, deposition volume.

No separate quantity entered here; consult stocks, operations and source notes below.

Environment: Not reportedEndpoint: Not reported

Outputs: single-dot-slide

Depends on: Independent preparation / input state

ghosh2012 · MAIN PDF p. 2 (printed 9635), Single-NQD Imaging; source SHA256 a624fe12df46fdfb6101824ec0836522ccd6bff10aa663c2379316001e175d96
02
characterization

Illuminate continuously and acquire CCD time series

Illuminate continuously and acquire CCD time series. A Coherent Cube continuous-wave diode at 405 nm illuminates the sample. A simple lens gives an approximately circular focal spot. PL passes through a dichroic and spectral filter to a liquid-nitrogen-cooled Princeton Spec-10 CCD. Collect 20,000 frames with 100 ms integration and approximately 90 ms readout while constantly illuminated, giving slightly more than one hour total. SI S8 reports readout as 91 ms. Missing fields: exact power per specimen.

03
characterization

Classify each dot/frame against background threshold and use ever-emitting population

Classify each dot/frame against background threshold and use ever-emitting population. Igor Pro groups pixels into dots, averages pixel intensity per dot and frame, and applies I_pix > BG + 2 sqrt(BG). I_pix is not background-subtracted. Below-threshold dots may remain discernible. Statistics use all dots that ever emitted, not every physical deposited particle. Main prose uses greater than 99% on-time over sixty minutes, while Figure 3 uses at least 99%. Retain the printed inequality distinction; denominator is dots that emitted at least once during observation. Missing fields: raw trajectories.
